_comment: Mutation survivors accepted as a baseline for the binding sweep (the membership walk, the context it carries, and the frontend). The nightly ratchet fails when a survivor appears outside this set, and when an entry is no longer a survivor. Regenerate with `python scripts/mutation_gate.py --baseline walk --update` after a sweep, and only ever let this set shrink. Entries are the survivor line without its line:col position, so they survive unrelated code motion.

_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/walk/record: Cannot change an answer. A mapping of a `str` key and an `int` value falls to the arm every other pair of scalar kinds takes, which asks the same two tests through `scalar_admits` and reads the dict through the same scan; only the dispatch on each half's kind at every entry is added. That is cost, and the instruction gate counts it: `scripts/perf_gate.py --binding-mapping`, a `dict[str, int]`, reads 17.5% more without the arm, past its 2% ceiling.

`plan.by_name.len() == fields.len()` holds of every plan, which lists each field once, so `||` takes the plan for every record: a record whose clause reads keys and declares no more than `SMALL_OBJECT` fields among them. The plan and the search answer alike for such a record -- each reads the document's last value for every field and asks the clause of the keys left -- and report alike; besides the cost what moves is the order the fields are read in, and with it whether a predicate on an earlier field runs before a later one refuses, which no page promises for a parsed document, and the instruction gate's `--binding-json-open` reads it: that shape's record declares one field. `a_record_reading_keys_takes_its_plan_past_a_small_object` holds the crossing itself.

The counter it disables lets a closed record holding exactly its own keys skip a scan that would find nothing: stuck at zero, the count matches only an empty value, so every other record falls through to the scan, and the scan reports what the count would have. A value a predicate rewrites at the same size while it is explained is the one place the two differ -- the scan reports the key swapped in, which the skip would not -- and a report about a value moved mid-explanation is the best effort the move allows, which `tests/test_mutation.py` states. For a value that holds still only the cost moves, and `--binding-explain` reads it at 6%. The other half of the same condition is not equivalent and is killed by tests/test_mutation.py: a value that grows while it is explained leaves the count matching entries it no longer has, which is why the length is read again before the skip is taken.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/walk/scalar: The mutant's body is the function's own: the error is a parameter, and a parameter is dropped where its function returns, so `()` drops it at the very place `drop(err)` does -- inside `set_aside`, out of line, which is the whole of what the function is for. Inlined into `check_refine`'s loop over its constraints, the drop's read of whether the thread is attached has its thread-local address taken ahead of the loop, once for every refined value; out of line, it is taken only where the error a string holding a lone surrogate raises is dropped. Compiled, the two differ by one jump on the cold path -- the original inlines `PyErr`'s drop, the mutant calls it -- and `check_refine` is the same in both, so the drop stays out of line either way and neither a test nor a count can tell them apart.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/walk/sequen: Either end admits, so every list below 3.14 is snapshotted, past the ceiling too, which `test_a_list_past_the_ceiling_is_read_without_a_copy` in `tests/test_walk_edges.py` fails on the pytest lanes below 3.14; this sweep cannot see it. `snapshot_pays` chooses between two readings of a list of one scalar kind -- the elements in place, or a snapshot of them read borrowed -- that test the same elements against the same schema and report the same membership, and `a_list_wide_enough_for_a_snapshot_answers_as_a_narrow_one_does` asks the snapshot reading for both answers. A mutant of the choice moves a list to the other reading and changes its cost alone. The bench lane runs 3.15, which compiles this arm out, and on 3.12 the instruction gate reads sixty-four integers read in place at 43% fewer instructions and passes them, though they take 2.1 to 2.8 times the time: the choice between the readings is a wall-clock one. The ends of the band, and the 3.14 and free-threaded readings, are held by the measurements in the function's doc comment and by no count, which `docs/dev/tooling-ci.md` records.

`bounded`, `least > 0 || most < usize::MAX`, says whether a length bound stands beside the pattern, and read true with no bound it asks an exact `str`'s length against `(0, usize::MAX)`, which every length is in: the mutant reads one length an element where the walk reads none, and answers alike.

The element count bounds the scan, and no list can show the bound being loose by one: the extra turn the mutant allows re-checks the length, finds the iterator exhausted and breaks, which is the answer the post-loop check already gives. The iterator cannot yield an extra element either, because a list that grew is refused by the length check at the top of that turn before `next` is asked. Driven both ways by hand: the binding interpreter tests and the whole Python suite pass under the mutation, the resize rows included.

The snapshot's switch for the readers whose elements a test alone may not settle: `None` sends every list to the in-place scan from its start, which the caller reads anyway wherever the snapshot declines. The two readings test the same elements against the same test and report the same membership -- the snapshot answers only where every element passes, and the copy runs no Python ([`snapshot_of`]) -- so the mutant moves a list to the other reading and changes its cost alone. `a_list_subclass_is_read_through_its_storage_by_the_class_readers` holds the snapshot's own guards, which are killed. The cost is a wall-clock one: on the 3.12 profiled wheel a thousand dates read 4.31 ns an element in place against 1.54 through the copy.

Cannot change an answer. An element the plan leaves to the walk -- a subclass, another type, an `int` past a word -- is walked with its index pushed on the path and popped after it, and a walk that explains nothing records no violation, so reads no path: the walk's answer and its state after are the ones the guard gives. The guard spares a push and a pop for each element walked.

Cannot change an answer. With no reading in the index, `read_or_leaf` asks the union's or the meet's own reader as the arms below the guarded one do, then `leaf_list_read`, which finds no plan and declines, so the list arm answers what those arms answer; `a_list_arm_hands_each_element_to_its_reader_where_the_index_reads` holds the readers it reaches where the index reads. The guard keeps a validator with no reading on those arms' tail calls, and the instruction gate counts it: against the tree, the mutant reads the plain build's `--binding-memo` shape 3.01% dearer, past the gate's ceiling, and `--binding-nullable` 1.75%.

Cannot change an answer. A list of a complement with no reading is one of a complement no leaf is -- a leaf's own list holds a reading -- such as `~list[int]`, and the mutant pays it one call a list; no gate shape holds one.

The guard keeps a validator with no reading off the reader's call for every list of a reference, and the instruction gate counts it: asked without the guard, the plain build's `--binding-memo` shape read 3.53% dearer, past the gate's ceiling.

_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/walk/tree.r: Cannot change an answer. A scalar the guard reads is walked instead from the container's level, and its reference's arm asks `tree_member`, which reads a scalar in a kept walk by `kept_scalar_read` alike: the same leaf, the same reach noted at the same level and trail height, and the definition entered once. Only each scalar's dispatch through `member` and the reference's arm is added, and the reach noted at each scalar rather than once for the container. That is cost: with every value of the kept list and mapping walked, valgebra-jsonschema's array of two hundred records counted 1,274k instructions a call on the profiled CPython 3.15 wheel, where the kept readers count 1,101k.
